title: Renormalization of One-Dimensional Semirelativistic Bosons with Contact Interactions
abstract: We study one-dimensional spinless bosons with semirelativistic spinless-Salpeter dispersion and attractive pairwise contact interactions. Because the dispersion becomes linear at large momentum, the contact interaction is marginal by power counting and produces a logarithmic ultraviolet divergence. We construct the renormalized many-body theory using an enlarged Fock space and a Schur-complement representation of the resolvent, eliminating the bare coupling in favor of the physical zero-total-momentum two-body bound-state energy. The resulting cutoff-independent resolvent defines a self-adjoint Hamiltonian in each fixed particle-number sector. We treat the two-body problem explicitly and show, in the norm-resolvent sense, that the nonrelativistic limit reproduces the attractive Lieb--Liniger Hamiltonian. We also formulate a mean-field approximation directly within the renormalized theory. In the massless and deeply bound large-particle-number regimes, it predicts an exponentially increasing binding scale whose exponent is determined by a one-dimensional variational problem.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a renormalization scheme for one-dimensional bosons with semirelativistic dispersion and contact interactions. By systematically handling logarithmic divergences using advanced resolvent techniques, the authors prove that the full interacting Hamiltonian converges to the established Lieb-Liniger model in the nonrelativistic limit. This provides a powerful, rigorous framework for studying strongly interacting quantum gases.
main_problem: The paper addresses the renormalization of a quantum many-body system consisting of one-dimensional spinless bosons interacting via attractive contact potentials, which leads to ultraviolet divergences.
main_result: The theory successfully constructs a cutoff-independent, self-adjoint Hamiltonian whose nonrelativistic limit precisely reproduces the well-known attractive Lieb-Liniger Hamiltonian.
method: The methodology involves advanced renormalization group techniques using an enlarged Fock space and the Schur-complement representation of the resolvent to systematically absorb divergences.
model_or_system: The system models spinless bosons in one dimension with a semirelativistic dispersion relation ($\hat{p}^2 + m^2$) and attractive contact interactions ($\delta(x)$). The Hamiltonian is studied in the context of quantum field theory renormalization.
key_observables: The zero-total-momentum two-body bound-state energy ($E_B$), the renormalized resolvent $R(E)$, and the mean-field binding scale $|E_{MF}|$.
important_parameters: The bare coupling constant ($\lambda$), the particle number ($N$), and the momentum cutoff ($\Lambda$ or $c$).
main_assumptions: The procedure assumes the existence of a unique self-adjoint Hamiltonian defined by the resolvent, and convergence is established by comparing the semirelativistic result to the known Lieb-Liniger model.
figures_summary: The notes reference mathematical equations (e.g., Eq. 1.1, Eq. 5.15, Eq. C.102) detailing the formal structure of the Hamiltonians, resolvents, and convergence proofs, rather than describing visual figures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the divergent Hamiltonian and the renormalization procedure (using the resolvent) to explicitly calculating the two-body sector, and finally demonstrating the convergence of the full $N$-body theory to the nonrelativistic Lieb-Liniger model.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, field-theoretic approach to handling strong, short-range interactions in low-dimensional quantum systems, connecting a relativistic-like dispersion to a standard nonrelativistic model (Lieb-Liniger).
